title: Ruby Concurrency
intro: Ruby concurrency interviews divide into two layers: the MRI GVL (Global VM Lock, often called GIL) which is the foundational constraint, and the concurrency primitives built on top of it — Thread, Mutex, Fiber, and the newer Ractor introduced in Ruby 3. The GVL means MRI threads cannot execute Ruby code in true parallel, but they do release the lock during IO — which is why Puma can serve multiple requests concurrently with threads even under MRI. This page covers Thread lifecycle and safety, Mutex.synchronize, the cooperative Fiber model, Ractor's share-nothing approach to true parallelism, the async gem for event-driven IO over Fibers, and the practical question engineers actually face: when to use Puma threads vs Unicorn processes for your Rails app workload.
